subject: Interim status: edge-region performance spike (US-West) & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@zephyrex.com>, ops@zephyrex.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interim status: edge-region performance spike (US-West) & next steps

Hi Maria / Zephyrex ops team,

Quick update to acknowledge the issue you reported: starting ~08:55 PDT we saw an elevated rate of 5xx responses and tail latency spikes affecting hosted inference in the US-West edge region. We’ve opened an incident (INC-20260815-usw) and posted an interim note on the status page: https://status.redwood.inference.com/incidents/INC-20260815-usw.

What we know so far:
- Symptom: transient 503/502 responses and 2–3x median latency on text generation endpoints for a subset of customers routed to US-West.
- Scope: ~5% of production requests, concentrated on models with long prefix sequences.
- Start time: 2026-08-15 08:55 PDT.
- Current mitigation: routing policy updated to send affected requests to standby capacity (reduces throughput but lowers errors).

What we’re doing next (short-term):
- Investigating autoscaler decisions and model-variant routing logs (Markus + Neha on this).
- Collecting representative traces and sample request IDs for your team to correlate.
- Rolling a config rollback if error rates don’t decline in the next 30 minutes.

We’ve attached initial logs for visibility (initial-incident-log.txt). I’ll follow up with a concise timeline and root-cause hypothesis once we have it.

I’m sorry for the disruption — we know this impacts your user-facing flows. Please let us know if you want us to route your entire account to a cold standby in a different region while we investigate.

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Lead Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-08-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Interim status: edge-region performance spike (US-West) & next steps

Internal notes (for the incident channel and runbook):

Forwarding Maria’s reply — they asked for routing to US-East and request IDs. Markus/Neha: can you prioritize trace collection for sample request IDs 7621f3b2 / 7621f3b7 (extracted from edge gateway) and check autoscaler logs for the period 08:50–09:10 PDT? Hypothesis: we’re seeing an unusual sequence-length distribution that caused the scheduler to consolidate KV cache allocations and overload a subset of inference nodes; this led to OOM/retry cascades and partial 503s.

Immediate actions taken:
- Routing policy updated to route Zephyrex to US-East per request.
- Increased standby pool for US-West to accept spillover for pinned customers.
- Captured kernel traces and host-level metrics; attaching notes.

Attachment: investigation-notes.pdf (internal).

If we confirm autoscaler misclassification, we should push a hotfix to the scaling heuristic and add a regression test for long-prefix traffic shapes.

— Dylan
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@zephyrex.com>, ops@zephyrex.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — US-West performance spike (INC-20260815-usw)

Hi Maria,

Thank you again for the patience while we investigated. Below is a concise post-incident summary and the actions we’ve taken. I’ve included the full timeline and a short-term mitigation plan; the attached postmortem has more detail.

Summary / root cause (brief):
- Root cause: a regression in the autoscaler heuristic that misclassified a sustained uptick in long-prefix requests as uniform low-latency traffic. This caused multiple GPU instances to be consolidated into fewer nodes for efficiency, creating transient memory pressure on KV cache hot-shards. Several inference workers rejected requests (503) when the KV cache allocation hit edge conditions.
- Contributing factors: lack of a synthetic test for long-prefix sequence distributions in the autoscaler CI, and a routing fallback configuration that delayed fallback by 30s (too long for this pattern).

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-08-15 08:55 PDT — first elevated error rate observed.
- 2026-08-15 09:12 PDT — initial customer notification sent.
- 2026-08-15 09:20 PDT — routing policy adjusted; Zephyrex traffic moved to US-East.
- 2026-08-15 10:00 PDT — error rates reduced to baseline.
- 2026-08-17 11:30 PDT — mitigation verified; fix plan scoped.

What we changed (short-term):
- Reverted autoscaler heuristic to previous stable version and deployed a guardrail to prevent consolidation on long-prefix models.
- Reduced fallback delay from 30s to 5s for edge region routing policies.
- Added request-ID logging for all fallback events for easier customer correlation.

Actions we will take (next 30 days):
- Ship a regression test for long-prefix traffic shapes into autoscaler CI (INF-4729).
- Add a synthetic load test targeting KV cache hot-shard behavior.
- Credit: we will apply a service credit for the period of elevated errors; my team will send the credit notification and calculation by 2026-08-20.

Attachments: postmortem-summary.pdf (includes detailed logs, corrective actions, and follow-up roadmap).

If you’d like a short call to walk through the postmortem and timeline, I’m available tomorrow morning PST. Otherwise, we’ll keep the incident page updated and close the incident once you confirm impact is resolved from your side.

Apologies again for the interruption; we’re prioritizing preventing recurrence.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Lead Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
